visualContract: Schematic educational mapping on a stylized procedural model; not atlas registration or live activity
disclaimer: Music uses overlapping distributed networks. A selectable region means explore research associations, NOT activate or target that brain structure. Internal structures are indicated by symbolic external markers.

regions.name: Auditory cortex
regions.evidence: Human neuroimaging and lesion studies implicate auditory cortex in pitch perception and musical sound processing; exact keys do not correspond to unique cortical targets.

regions.name: Supplementary motor area
regions.topic: Internal beat timing and motor prediction
regions.evidence: A meta-analysis of 30 fMRI studies found supplementary motor area involvement in musical rhythm. Tempo alone cannot guarantee its response.

source.title: Identifying a brain network for musical rhythm (2022)

regions.name: Cerebellum
regions.evidence: Rhythm complexity and sensorimotor synchronization involve cerebellar networks; no direct BPM-to-cerebellum activation mapping exists.

source.title: From Sound to Movement: Auditory-Motor Entrainment Review

regions.name: Putamen / basal ganglia
regions.location: Subcortical — INTERNAL; external marker is conceptual
regions.topic: Beat tracking, tempo prediction and internal pulse
regions.evidence: Meta-analysis associates beat-based rhythm processing with bilateral putamen. The external marker does NOT indicate the structure's true cortical-surface location.

source.title: Musical rhythm: meta-analysis of 30 functional studies

regions.name: Inferior frontal gyrus
regions.topic: Harmonic structure, expectation and musical syntax
regions.evidence: Inferior frontal and temporal networks process musical harmonic dependencies; C major, D minor, and other named keys are not individually brain-targeting.

source.title: Neural networks for harmonic structure in music perception and action

regions.name: Music reward network
regions.location: Deep nucleus accumbens/striatum — symbolic outside marker
regions.topic: Individual pleasure, familiarity and motivational reward
regions.evidence: Individual listening pleasure has been linked to mesolimbic structures in neuroimaging, but a song's BPM/key alone cannot predict or induce reward, and no user is diagnosed.

methods.metaanalysis: Strength of evidence relates to research consistency, never probability of activation for one listener.
methods.individualDifference: Responses vary by task, training, familiarity, hearing status, context and individual characteristics; data have not been gathered in this interface.
methods.markers: Approximate illustration positions, not stereotaxic coordinates or medical localization.
